title: Clathrate hydrate dissociation curves and eutectic brines (GEN.471)

sources.marboeuf-2014: Marboeuf et al. 2014, section 3.4 and Table 5 (from Hersant 2004): ln P_cl(Pa) = A0 + A1/T for the hydrates in the cold ice regime; hydrate number 6 for all; CO, CO2, CH4, H2S form structure I, N2 structure II, NH3 a stoichiometric monohydrate (read by the Body composition research lane, part C)
sources.semenov-2023: Semenov, Int. J. Mol. Sci. 24, 9321 (DOI 10.3390/ijms24119321): CO2 hydrate quadruple points Q1 (V-Lw-I-H) 271.60 K at 1.044 MPa (+/- 0.023 K, +/- 0.021 MPa) and Q2 (V-Lw-L-H) 283.13 K at 4.494 MPa
sources.chevrier-2009: Chevrier, Hanley and Altheide 2009, GRL 36, L10202 (Crossref abstract read): eutectics of 206 +/- 1 K at 44.0 wt% Mg(ClO4)2 and 236 +/- 1 K at 52 wt% NaClO4
sources.pestova-2005: Pestova et al. 2005 and Marion et al. 2010 (Icarus 207, 675), as quoted by Martinez et al. arXiv:1811.00862 and Rivera-Valentin et al. arXiv:2012.00100 (second-hand): Ca(ClO4)2 eutectic 198 to 199 K, water activity 0.51 to 0.52
sources.parametrisation: the linear liquidus between pure water and the eutectic, the eutectic spread (the stated plus or minus) and the water activity of an arbitrary mixture are parametrisations of this module

Mg(ClO4)2.limit: authors differ: 205 K (Gough 2011) to 212 K (Pal and Kereszturi); the water activity 0.55 to 0.56 is second-hand

Ca(ClO4)2.limit: second-hand (arXiv preprints quoting Pestova 2005 and Marion 2010); the eutectic composition was not reached
